Our licensed technicians serve residential and commercial properties across Manhasset — call (855) 930-5016 for a free phone quote and clear pricing before any work begins.
whyUs: With years of experience serving Long Island communities, Best Pest Control NYC combines local expertise with proven bee removal techniques to deliver safe, effective results. Our licensed technicians understand Manhasset's unique property layouts and respond quickly to bee infestations in this prestigious North Shore community.
localContext: Manhasset's tree-lined streets, historic estates near Shelter Rock Road, and upscale properties around Plandome Road provide ideal nesting sites for wasps, hornets, and yellow jackets in eaves, soffits, chimneys, and wall voids. The area's proximity to Manhasset Bay, mature landscaping, and gardens around the Northern Boulevard shopping district create year-round pressure from stinging insects seeking protected cavities. Carpenter bees bore into exposed wood trim and fascia on older estates, while ground-nesting yellow jackets colonize lawn edges and garden beds.

faqs.question: How quickly can you treat a wasp or hornet nest in my Manhasset property?
faqs.answer: We offer same-day or next-day service in Manhasset depending on availability. Active wasp and hornet nests inside wall voids or high-traffic areas are urgent — we prioritize rapid response to eliminate the threat and seal entry points before the colony grows.

faqs.question: What does the wasp and hornet removal service include?
faqs.answer: Every service includes species identification, locating the nest entrance, direct treatment of the nest, removal of accessible nest material, and sealing every opening to prevent recolonization. Carpenter bee treatments include residual dust applied into the galleries and wood sealant to close the holes. Ground nests are treated at night when the colony is inactive.

faqs.question: Do you treat honeybees in Manhasset?
faqs.answer: No, we do not treat honeybees. If an inspection confirms a colony is honeybees rather than wasps or hornets, we refer the situation to a licensed beekeeper instead of treating it ourselves.
